claims.text: Overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by thermally induced Cu segregation.
Thermally induced Cu segregation produces a continuous Cu-rich tribofilm at the sliding interface.
The Cu-rich tribofilm accommodates plastic deformation.
The Cu-rich tribofilm lowers interfacial shear.
Formation of the Cu-rich tribofilm reduces wear relative to a coating without Cu segregation.
Formation of the Cu-rich tribofilm reduces underlying microstructural damage relative to a coating without Cu segregation.
The baseline coating is defined as having a relatively homogeneous elemental distribution without pronounced Cu segregation.
Thermal treatment or sliding exposure at approximately 400–600 °C will accelerate Cu diffusion and segregation toward the coating surface.
Sliding-induced stresses promote formation of a continuous Cu-rich surface layer from segregated Cu.
The Cu-rich layer produces a more ductile, accommodated interfacial deformation mode.
The thermally treated coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline coating.
The thermally treated coating will have reduced wear-track depth relative to the baseline coating.
The thermally treated coating will show a continuous Cu-enriched surface layer.
The thermally treated coating will show fewer abrasive-wear features.
The thermally treated coating will show fewer adhesive-wear features.
The thermally treated coating will show a more ductile and continuous microscopic deformation pattern at the interface.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold during sliding at approximately 400–600 °C under significant interfacial stress.
The proposed behavior may not apply at lower temperatures or without significant sliding-induced interfacial stress.

contradictions.description: Elevated-temperature sliding at 400–600 °C is itself offered as an intervention that induces Cu segregation, yet the nominally untreated baseline is to be tested under identical temperature and sliding conditions while being assumed to retain minimal surface Cu enrichment. Without a distinct pretreatment or another controlled difference, both groups may receive the proposed segregation-inducing exposure.
